header: This is a standalone model adapter (Groq's OpenAI-compatible endpoint). I deliberately do NOT import the app's ai-services.ts, so the experiment stays isolated and can run from a plain command line. It has the same model default and call shape as the app's own working Groq call.

params.name: opts
params.type: { maxTokens?: number; maxWaitSeconds?: number; onUsage?: (u: TokenUsage) => void }

doc: Groq adapter. Everything below is read at CALL time from the environment, and every lever is OFF unless you set it: GROQ_MODEL the main model (default openai/gpt-oss-120b) GROQ_FALLBACK_MODELS comma-separated backups, used ONLY when the main model is rate-limited for more than ~2 s. Each Groq model has its OWN free allowance, so a backup answers at once instead of waiting. A backup may write weaker SQL than the main model: measure it with eval/run-live.ts first. GROQ_REASONING_EFFORT low | medium | high -- how much a reasoning model "thinks" (less = fewer tokens, faster) Every call prints one line with the tokens it used, so you can see how close the day's allowance is.

doc: Gemini adapter with the same LlmFn shape as groqLlm. The model answers JSON only (the NL2SQL pipeline parses JSON). I set thinking to "low": SQL writing needs a little reasoning, not a lot, and a large thinking budget makes every employee question slow and dearer. GEMINI_CHAT_MODEL main model (default gemini-3.8-flash); falls back to gemini-flash-latest.
